summary: Iter 8: PayPal Orders v2 REST integration verified end-to-end in unconfigured state. Extended backend suite from 52 → 56 tests (added 4 PayPal endpoint tests + updated billing/methods shape test to expect 3 gateways). All 56 tests pass (100%). Frontend Pricing page verified: grid-cols-3 with opt-stripe, opt-razorpay (dim opacity=0.5), opt-paypal (dim opacity=0.5); both razorpay-unavailable and paypal-unavailable notices render simultaneously; unlock-btn labelled 'Unlock lifetime · $1'; geo=US, paid-price=$1. Regressions all green: Stripe checkout, semantic pdf-search, all 45 non-search tools, auth, user_jobs, razorpay 503s.

When real PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are provided, re-run iter 8 tests — the 503 assertions in test_paypal_order/capture_503_when_unconfigured will need to be flipped to real order/400 tests. paypal_webhook_ignored also becomes 200 with signature-verified path.
critical_code_review_comments: paypal_gw.py: capture endpoint returns 400 on any PayPal error (including a well-formed 404 bad-order-id) — acceptable per spec. Idempotent grant guarded by `payment_status != paid` conditional update — good.
paypal_gw.py: uses user['_id'] in reference_id and PayPal-Request-Id — ensures idempotency across retries. Good.

paypal_gw.py: webhook returns {status:'ignored'} when unavailable (200 OK) — matches spec; when configured and PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID unset it silently skips verification and processes events. Consider requiring PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID when paypal_available()==True to avoid a spoofable ingestion path in production.
server.py /billing/methods: recommended order (razorpay for IN → stripe → paypal → null) is fine; PayPal never becomes 'recommended' unless both Stripe and Razorpay are down.

Pricing.jsx: opt-razorpay/opt-paypal use opacity=0.5 CSS visual disable but no `disabled` attr on the underlying button — selection is prevented via `available` check inside GatewayOption. That's fine for a11y as long as aria-disabled is also set (verify).
